memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpah, Kephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Haeleph, the Jebusite city (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeah and Kiriath—fourteen towns and their villages. This was the inheritance of Benjamin for its clans - Josh 18:25-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The final group of Benjamin's towns is listed, fourteen in all, closing the chapter's account of this tribe's inheritance. And tucked into the list is a name we have seen before: "the Jebusite city (that is, Jerusalem)." Once again the future holy city appears, still in enemy hands, listed among Benjamin's towns as an inheritance not yet fully possessed.

How patient God is in His unfolding plan. Jerusalem sits quietly in this list, giving no hint of the glory that would one day fill it — the city of David, the site of the temple, the place where Jesus would die and rise. What appears now as merely "the Jebusite city," an unconquered corner, God was reserving for the very centre of His redemptive work. The greatest things were still ahead for this ordinary-sounding name.

This is a comfort when we look at the unfinished, unpromising corners of our own lives. God sees what a place — or a person — can become long before it is realised. The situation that looks like nothing but a problem today may be exactly where God intends to do something significant tomorrow. He is never in a hurry, and He never overlooks. The Jebusite city became the city of God. In the same way, God is patiently working His purposes in the ordinary and unfinished places of our lives, for His glory and our good (Phil 1:6).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What "unconquered corner" of your life feels unpromising right now?
- How does God's long plan for Jerusalem encourage you to be patient?
- Do you trust that God sees what your situation can become?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You see what ordinary and unfinished places can become. Help me to be patient and to trust that You are working Your good purposes even in the unpromising corners of my life. Amen.
